source: Secure Prompt Assistant guidance table (cwe_guidance.yaml), exported by scripts/export_lint_data.py

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is formatted into the SQL text passed to `{sink}`.
templates.directive: Use a parameterised query: put a placeholder in the SQL text and pass `{source}` separately as a bound parameter of `{sink}`.
templates.guard: The query may run only after `{source}` is bound as a parameter; never build SQL text from it.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is concatenated into a command that `{sink}` runs through a shell.
templates.directive: Call the program with an argument list and shell=False, passing `{source}` as a single argument, and reject values that do not match a strict allowlist pattern.
templates.guard: Run the command only if `{source}` has passed the allowlist check; never pass it through a shell.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is inserted into an HTML response without escaping.
templates.directive: HTML-escape `{source}` before it is placed in the response, for example with markupsafe.escape or a template with autoescaping.
templates.guard: Insert `{source}` into the HTML only after it has been escaped.

templates.explain: `{target}` holds a credential written directly in the source code.
templates.directive: Remove the literal value and load `{target}` at runtime from an environment variable or a secret manager.
templates.guard: Use the credential only if it was supplied at runtime; fail with a clear error when it is missing instead of falling back to a default.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is joined into a filesystem path that `{sink}` opens.
templates.directive: Resolve the joined path and refuse the request unless the resolved path stays inside `{base}`, for example with os.path.realpath and os.path.commonpath.
templates.guard: Open the file only if the resolved path is inside `{base}`; otherwise return an error.

templates.explain: `{sink}` is a fast, unsalted hash, so it is unsuitable for protecting `{source}`.
templates.directive: Hash `{source}` with a slow, salted password-hashing function such as hashlib.scrypt or PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a random per-password salt.
templates.guard: Store or compare a password only after it has been through the salted password-hashing function.

templates.explain: `{sink}` generates a security-sensitive value but is not a cryptographically secure generator.
templates.directive: Generate the value with the secrets module (for example secrets.token_urlsafe or secrets.randbelow) instead of `{sink}`.
templates.guard: Issue the value only when it comes from a cryptographically secure generator.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is passed to `{sink}`, which can execute code while deserialising.
templates.directive: Do not unpickle client data; parse `{source}` as JSON with json.loads and validate the expected fields.
templates.guard: Accept the data only after it has been parsed as plain JSON and its fields validated.

templates.explain: `{sink}` is called with debug mode switched on in the code.
templates.directive: Do not enable debug mode in code; read the setting from configuration, such as an environment variable, that defaults to off.
templates.guard: Enable debugging only when it is explicitly configured for local development, never by default.

templates.explain: `{package}` is pinned to version {version}, which has known vulnerabilities ({vulns}).
templates.directive: Upgrade `{package}` to {fixed} or later and keep the version pinned exactly.
templates.guard: Deploy only after `{package}` is at a version that fixes {vulns}.
